h.strategy: Use retrieved findings to identify which settings are strong, weak or neutral, and which parts can be cut off from the outcome by other settings. Build hypotheses mainly from (a) the edited field's current value in the parent, since replacing a strong value with a weak one hurts and filling an empty or harmful slot helps, and (b) conditions that disconnect the edited part, which shrink its effect. When finding flaws, replace any hypothesis whose direction could plausibly reverse because of a competing effect, or whose mechanism relies on partial redundancy between different parts. Ensure varied edit fields and values. State a one-sentence mechanism.

hyps.why: With edge 0 removed, node 1 has no input, so a conv on edge 1->2 processes nothing and has little effect.
A conv on edge 1->3 is disconnected from the input when edge 0 is none, so its benefit shrinks.
Edge 2->3 being none cuts the output of edge 1->2 from the cell output, so edits to it matter less.
With edge 5 none, node 2 cannot reach the output, so improving edge 0->2 has little effect.
Edge 1->3 is fed by nothing when edge 0 is none, so improving it barely changes the output.
A disconnected edge 2->3 isolates edge 1->2 from the output, shrinking the edit's effect.
Node 2 is cut off from the output when edge 5 is none, so changing edge 0->2 matters less.
Filling an empty output edge with a strong conv gains more than replacing any existing op.
Adding a conv to an empty edge gains more than swapping it for an existing operation.
An empty first edge starves node 1, so putting a conv there gives a large gain.
